answer: The papermaker sorts every rag before it enters the vat and enters the sorting in his book against the ream it becomes. A meadow sheet bought from another mill fails the book: at the pearl of the rag the fibres must match the papermaker's own sorting, and strange paper yellows within a year. Forging a ream means hiring a papermaker, buying false rags and paying 11,500, and the walnut line in the sorting book is read at every court, so a sheet whose rags were never sorted is burned.
